latest.notes:
Logs now build in two phases: stop sets first, then music.

Press Regenerate and you will see the break skeleton appear first — stop sets, imaging, voice tracks and segments, with no music at all. The commercial log fills those breaks. Only then is the music scheduled, into the time that is actually left.

This is what you have been asking for, and it removes the whole class of problem rather than correcting for it afterwards. Music is never scheduled against a break length that turns out to be wrong, so songs are not placed and then thrown away — they stay in rotation.

The music pass no longer depends on the commercial fill succeeding. If the fill fails, the hours are sized against unfilled breaks and the report says so plainly, rather than the music silently staying as first laid out.

Generating is also quicker, because the first pass no longer picks music it is about to discard.
